advisory.finding: The run_chunk seam catches every `LLMError`, so verifier-side failures are counted as provider outages. These include StructuredOutputError (the verifier's turn failed the `verification` contract), RunawayToolLoopError (an agentic tool loop), LLMInputRejectedError and LLMBudgetExhaustedError. A run that fails this way is filed under `unavailable`, and the test then fails with 'the provider failed N/3 runs, so verifier behavior was not measured'. The diff exists to tell an outage apart from verifier misbehavior, so this label points the maintainer at an outage when the verifier (the unit these tests measure) is actually misbehaving.
scenarios: The agentic code-review verifier gets stuck in a tool loop on 2 of 3 runs and RunawayToolLoopError is raised. The test fails saying the provider failed and behavior was not measured, so the failure is treated as a transient outage and retried or ignored.

A prompt change makes the verifier emit an invalid `verification` shape and StructuredOutputError is raised. This is the behavioral regression these tests exist to catch, but the failure message blames the provider.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `except LLMError as exc:` with `except LLMUnavailableError as exc:` (import from rebar.llm.errors) in the run_chunk of all three modules. The commit message describes the Bedrock 503 as surfacing as LLMUnavailableError. Other LLMError subclasses then propagate to verify_findings' degrade/contract-violation path without being labelled as outages.
